posts.author: Jeffrey Weil
posts.content_md:
Hello John,

That's steel pipe, I think 1 1/2. Those are key clamps. They have a hex screw that bears down on the outside of the pipe. If that were pvc it could never take the stress. Or, the key clamps would be glued in. They are more expensive than the same connectors in pvc which would glue better. 

Has to be steel. 

Jeff W

posts.author: cnewswanger
posts.content_md:
I've used these tubing clamps successfully many times.

I've built some large structures as well.

Here's a link to McMaster Carr:

[http://www.mcmaster.com/#catalog/117/1914/=e4p5z4](http://www.mcmaster.com/#catalog/117/1914/=e4p5z4)

Note the actual pipe diameter for "1 1/2" pipe is actually 1 7/8".

The clamps are expensive but you will likely reuse the clamps for many set-ups.

If you use "adjustable angle tee's" make sure you can tighten the swivel joint with a bolt. Some have a pin that allows some wiggle.

Wiggle = bad.

When i've had moving parts on the table I often filled the tubes with sand to help dampen out vibrations.

I made wood plugs from dowel which I epoxied into place.

Cheers,

Craig

posts.author: John Sonley
posts.content_md:
Hi - here's my version of my overhead reference beam made from KeeKlamp fittings. The set-up as shown is for H1 master transmission holograms. Also in view is the large plano-convex collimating mirror I use in making 5" X 8" masters. 

The overhead mirror is set so that the reference beam strikes the film plate at 56 deg plate normal, this angle together with a half wave plate in the beam gets rid of woodgraining in the glass/film/glass dry filmholder 'sandwiches' I use to support my film for exposure.

I've now made some very bright and successful H1s, so this construction passes the stability test

I'll be re-jigging the whole set-up quite soon to turn my H1s into Image Plane H2s

posts.author: John Sonley
posts.content_md:
> **Kiffdino:** so cool , that thing looks like a spaceship. and everything on a sand table. like it has landed on some remote planet.

KeeKlamp is great stuff for making this type of structure - there is a wide selection of fitments, ideally suited to the heavy engineering necessary with holographic overhead structures - but it's heavy stuff when the structure becomes large and a coat or two of spirit based blackboard paint (high in VOCs) gives a good looking matt black finish.

My reason for stressing this type of paint is that I've noticed the 'green' water based paint gives a shiny black finish- not what I wnted!

posts.author: John Klayer
posts.content_md: I attached one end to a magnet and slid it X-Y around in the beam till I got the most light out the other end. I just used whatever came out the other end for the reference, no other optics. I have tried getting fancy by using a space filter movement but the sliding magnet is good enough.
